primary_claim: Ablating a single 'superweight' in OLMo-1B causes perplexity to spike from 17.4 to 2884.3 with pathological outputs, but training a single trainable row-vector patch via KL distillation from the original model recovers approximately 93% of the lost performance while learning a new, largely orthogonal distributed direction rather than relearning the original weight (cosine similarity to the original row ~0.13).
limitations_stated: severe compute constraints (CPU-only) limited training to only two epochs / 400 optimization steps
quote: Surprisingly, it worked! Perplexity dropped drastically(i.e 2884.3 to 25.2) nearing the original model's values, and the Tokyo prompt was fixed... I observed approximately 93% recovery.
